messages:
ranjit: quick question — we just hit a case in canary where requests with an empty Authorization header plus an X-Project header were accepted. can we confirm intended behavior?

amelia: oof. what did the backend decide to do (401 vs 403 vs fallback)?

ranjit: backend returned 200 and routed to the org tied to X-Project. traffic test showed ~0.2% of requests had Authorization: '' (empty string) from a legacy SDK.

joyce: security standpoint: empty auth should be treated as missing -> 401. we shouldn't silently accept.

kai: SDK note: older python SDK did a header set even when token was empty. we fixed it in v1.4.2 but users may still be on older versions.

sam: product question — is there any case we intentionally allow X-Project to authenticate when Authorization absent? I thought project-level fallback is only for internal org proxies.

amelia: right — fallback to X-Project is only allowed when the request comes from an internal ingresses list and has a trusted proxy ip. the canary was coming from a public LB, so that should have failed.

ranjit: reproduction snippet from the canary logs:
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: 
X-Project: proj_ABC123
User-Agent: legacy-sdk/0.9
```
response: 200, model: r-3-small

joyce: can we add a server-side check: if Authorization header is present but length == 0 -> treat as missing and return 401? that prevents accidental acceptance.

amelia: +1. also add telemetry flag so we can count occurrences and link to SDK version via UA. we should not change existing fallback rules otherwise.

kai: I'll open an SDK issue to mark the orphaned header behavior and push a patch note. can we have a header-parsing unit test in the ingress code?

ranjit: I'll raise a runtime PR to reject empty Authorization and to 1) log telemetry event auth.empty_header_detected, 2) return 401 with body {"error":"missing credentials"} for empty/absent auth unless trusted-proxy override is in effect.

sam: for customer-impact, suggest we run a small rolling canary after the PR and keep a temporary whitelist for the legacy sdk user agents so we don't break enterprise customers unexpectedly.

joyce: whitelisting UA is risky. better approach: short grace window where we return 401 but include an `X-Auth-Deprecation` response header telling clients to upgrade, and send a weekly email to high-volume keys detected.

amelia: agree with joyce. Implementation plan:
- runtime change: treat empty Authorization as missing -> 401 (PR ready)
- add telemetry counter + UA sampling (kai)
- response header `X-Auth-Deprecation: empty-auth-will-be-rejected-2026-04-15` for 30 days
- create internal alert if auth.empty_header_detected > 1000/day (ops)

ranjit: timeline: I'll draft PR today, aim for canary tomorrow. kai, can you do the SDK issue and patch in the morning?

kai: yep. will also add a lint in the SDK CI to not set Authorization if token falsy.

ci-bot: deploy scheduled for canary slot 03:00 UTC. note: requires config flag `reject_empty_auth=true` enabled for canary.

sam: also — small API contract note for docs: clarify that empty Authorization is invalid and will result in 401; add example headers showing omission vs bearer.

ranjit: thanks all. I'll include the example curl in the PR and ping infra to ensure LB doesn't inject/strip X-Project.

joyce: one more: 401 vs 403 mapping for invalid token vs forbidden resource — ensure we keep semantics: invalid/missing -> 401, valid token but no project access -> 403. keep tests for both.

amelia: noted. I'll add unit tests for both paths and add an integration test that simulates proxy-with-xproject allowed only from internal IPs.

ranjit: great. will update thread when PR is up.
